Sustenance

• **Sustenance **refers to **the food and nourishment necessary to maintain life and health.** It can also refer to the **means of support or livelihood, both in a literal and figurative sense.**

 
 
• Example of sustenance: The refugees were in need of **sustenance **and shelter. - In this sentence, sustenance refers to the basic necessities required for survival, such as food, water, and shelter.
 
 
 
• **Aid **and **sustenance **are related words that have some overlap in meaning. Both words refer to forms of support or assistance that help someone or something to continue or survive.
 
• **Aid **can refer to** any type of help or support provided to someone or something in need, including financial, material, or physical support.** Sustenance, on the other hand, usually refers specifically** to food or other necessities that help a person or animal to survive.**
 
• However, in some contexts, the word sustenance can be used more broadly to refer to any type of support or assistance that helps to maintain something, such as a business or an ecosystem. In this sense, sustenance can be seen as a synonym of aid, as both words refer to forms of support that help something to continue or thrive.
 
 
• For example, a government might provide aid to a struggling business in the form of tax breaks or other financial incentives, which could be seen as a form of sustenance for the business. Similarly, a nonprofit organization might provide aid to support the ecological sustenance of a natural habitat or ecosystem.
 
 
 
• **"Extras"** and "Injury" are not synonyms of sustenance. **Extras **refers to **something additional or supplementary,** while injury refers to **harm or damage.**
 
• **"Blockage" **is also not a synonym of sustenance. **Blockage **refers to **an obstruction or barrier that prevents something from flowing or moving freely.**
 
• Hence, according to the meaning of the words, the correct answer is **'Aid'**

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

The goal of personal development is to learn and apply that (1)/which enable us to attain emotional well-being, understanding, and (2)/effectiveness, and to share this knowledge with others. (3)/No error (4)

**In part 2 of the sentence,** the usage of 'which' is incorrect.

 
• When the information is important and meaning-altering, we use ‘that.’ but if we are just adding extra information that’s not really needed, we will use ‘which.’ 
 
• Here, in the sentence, 'goals' of personal development and its application is discussed which makes the information important. Therefore, we will use 'That' instead of 'which'.
 
• **According to the rule of subject-verb agreement, **the verb of the sentence should be according to the subject. If the subject is plural then the verb should be plural on the other hand if the subject is singular then the verb should be singular.
 
• **In the given sentence,** the subject is 'goal' because 'of' is a preposition and 'personal development' is a prepositional phrase 'is' is used for the subject 'the goal'
 
• ***'to' **is a preposition and we know that with the preposition we always need a prepositional object which can be a noun/pronoun/gerund/noun clause/noun phrase. In this case, it is a noun clause in this clause the subject is 'learn and apply' which is in a plural form because two nouns are connected with the conjunction 'and' so the verb should be plural. So that's why 'enable' is used.*

**So the correct sentence is-** *The goal of personal development is to learn and apply **that **enable** **us to attain emotional well-being, understanding, and effectiveness, and to share this knowledge with others. *

questions.question: Disguised unemployment generally means________.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Disguised Unemployment:

 
 
• It is a phenomenon wherein more people are employed than actually needed.
 
• It is primarily traced to the agricultural and unorganised sectors of India.
 
• The marginal productivity of labour is zero.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Seasonal Unemployment:

 
 
• It is unemployment that occurs during certain seasons of the year.
 
• Agricultural labourers in India rarely have worked throughout the year.
 
 
 
• Structural Unemployment:
 
 
• It is a category of unemployment arising from the mismatch between the jobs available in the market and the skills of the available workers in the market.
 
• Many people in India do not get the job due to a lack of requisite skills and due to the poor education level, it becomes difficult to train them.
 
 
 
• Cyclical Unemployment:
 
 
• It is the result of the business cycle, where unemployment rises during recessions and declines with economic growth.
 
• Cyclical unemployment figures in India are negligible. It is a phenomenon that is mostly found in capitalist economies.
 
 
 
• Technological Unemployment:
 
 
• It is the loss of jobs due to changes in technology.
 
• In 2016, World Bank data predicted that the proportion of jobs threatened by automation in India is 69% year-on-year.
 
 
 
• Frictional Unemployment:
 
 
• Frictional Unemployment also called Search Unemployment, refers to the time lag between the jobs when an individual is searching for a new job or is switching between the jobs.

questions.question: According to Dr. Ambedkar which Article is the most important article of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32.**__

__
 
• **Article 32** is the** most important article** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 32 was called the** “soul of the constitution and very heart of it” **by **Dr Ambedkar.**
 
• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution gives the** right to individuals to move to the Supreme Court to seek justice when they feel that their right has been 'unduly deprived'****.​**
 
• It is also known as Right to Constitutional Remedies.

• This article** declares that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law.**
 
• This right is available to** both citizens and non-citizens.**
 
• The right to life is not merely confined to animal existence or survival but also includes the right to live with human dignity and all those aspects of life which go to make a man’s life meaningful, complete, and worth living.
 
 
 
• **Article 24 – Prohibition of employment of children in factories, etc.**
 
 
• Article 24 says that “No child below the age of fourteen years shall be employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment.”
 
• This Article forbids the employment of children below the age of 14 in any hazardous industry or factories or mines, without exception.
 
• However, the employment of children in non-hazardous work is allowed.

questions.question:
How is the nitrogen taken up by the plants?

I. In the form of inorganic nitrates or nitrites

II. In the form of organic compounds

III. Directly taken up from the atmosphere
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I and II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Plants take nitrogen from the soil by absorption through their **roots as nitrate ions, nitrite ions, or ammonium ions.**
 
• Most nitrogen obtained by terrestrial animals can be traced back to the eating of plants at some stage of the food chain.
 
• Plants take up nitrogen compounds through their roots. Nitrifying bacteria in the soil convert ammonia into nitrite (NO2 –) and then into nitrate (NO3 –). This process is called **nitrification**.
 
• Besides plants also take up nitrogen in **organic form Several organic compounds (compounds containing carbon) compose the organic fraction of nitrogen in the soil.**
 
• Soil organic matter exists as decomposing plant and animal residues, relatively stable products of decomposition-resistant compounds and humus.
 
• Plant roots themselves can affect the abundance of various forms of nitrogen by changing the pH and secreting organic compounds or oxygen.

questions.question: Which of the following relation is true regarding the amounts of genetic material contributed by the father and mother to the child?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Father = Mother**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A child inherits** EXACTLY 50% of the chromosomes from each of both parents.**
 
• All mitochondrial genes are inherited only from the mother.
 
• Thus a child receives only close to half of the genes from the father and a little bit more than half of the genes from the mother.
 
• This is achieved through sexual fertilization, requiring the meeting of the sperm with the egg, and the combining of the DNA from both (since the sperm and egg contain only half the genetic information in the parent).
 
• This ensures that families maintain some genetic identity, but also that a child must be genetically different from either parent or from any of their four grandparents.
